verdict.rationale: Gmail filters can route incoming mail by rule: they match criteria like sender, subject or size, then add labels or forward the message to a specified address, such as a teammate. Nothing documents assigning a conversation to a teammate or tracking who owns it. Delegation only grants mailbox access and does not assign ownership. missing for 10: conversation assignment to teammates, explicit ownership/assignee tracking, team-level routing rules (beyond per-account filters), independent corroboration.

support.subject: As a team-lead, I can assign conversations to teammates and route incoming mail with rules so ownership is explicit

citations.quote: When a message matches, filters automatically trigger actions such as adding or removing labels, or forwarding the email to a specified address.
Advanced rules configured for an account that evaluate incoming messages against specific matching criteria (like sender, subject, or size).
After you search, you can use the results to set up a filter for these messages.
